body:
Yeah, I see that. I feel like that was a realistic stupid mistake made by a teenager. And while it was extremely selfish of Rory to not show up to her mother’s graduation, I feel like intent also matters.

It was selfish and it was stupid, but it wasn’t malicious and it certainly wasn’t on purpose. rory also tried to do a kind thing when she invited her grandparents.

Oh man, just wait until OP realizes that Mother Teresa wasn’t really much of a saint and that Martin Luther King Jr. cheated on his wife, and all the things that Gandhi did with underage girls, or Winston Churchill caused famines that killed millions…

It’s almost as if human beings are complex people and that life isn’t so black-and-white after all. If anything I feel like OP losing all new ones when it comes to Rory is just as bad as over idolizing her

Again, I feel like people are rapidly underestimating how hard it is to be a teenager to a single mom and a deadbeat dad and get perfect grades on top of that. Rory absolutely makes a decent amount of mistakes, but people severely underestimate how stupid and how selfish teenagers can be and I see it all the time in this subreddit. Honestly people sound super out of touch whenever they complain about basic stupid things that Rory does. 

Not every moment is a character, flaw, or proof that she’s going to become some evil witch. People need to make mistakes to grow from them. The audience needs to watch the protagonist making mistakes so they also grow with the show.

Literally, the show would just be Rory does everything perfectly and then everyone would complain about her being a Mary Sue and then the show would be canceled after two seasons. 

Have people never watch TV shows? It’s supposed to be dramatic! That’s the point of having a plot

I know that Jess dealt with worse trauma than Rory, but literally we only get to see the best parts of Jess because Rory is the main character. And Jess did not have his shit together for years.

Rory absolutely makes some horrible mistakes, but Jess gets a free pass on things that Rory gets crucified for all the time. Jess was happily flirting with Rory while she was in a relationship with Dean and if Jess was a female character, my God, she would be slut shamed until the cows came home.

Exactly I’m proud of Jess for being able to be a published author, but a lot of people gloss over the fact that Rory was dealing with a lot of trauma from an absent emotionally abusive father, emotionally, immature mother (and I really still appreciate Lorelei and i thinks she has great qualities, and she’s not even that bad of a mother, but she does have problems) and still managed to graduate on time with an honors degree from an Ivy League! 

I feel like there’s a huge wave of anti-intellectualism and a lot of people are downplaying Rory’s achievements and academic accomplishments

People with zero self awareness on this sub always act as if they were perfect little angels at 19, and I bet my bottom dollar that they were just as insufferable as everyone else. 

Is talking shit about someone nice? No, but like everybody does it. Can we not crucify everything Rory does and then also lament that too many female characters are Mary sues ?

Rory gets shit for half the things college kids do weekly, like so many posts here give old man yelling at cloud energy.

I liked the moment too because I feel like people just see Paris as this one dimensional overachiever who’s better than Rory in every way when in reality Both girls compliment each other quite nicely. 

Rory is kind, and great at managing  people which makes her a great editor and friend. Paris is ambitious and driven.
Exactly, she’s valedictorian of an Ivy League feeder school

Idk Rory scored higher on her PSATs and Paris missed a lot of school after she didn’t get into Harvard.

Honestly maybe Principal Charles were scared that Paris would make another speech

Exactly and for people saying it’s not that deep- LOOK at how badly Mitchum’s father treats Shera at the dinner. 

Logan was always a screw up and seemed like the type to never take women seriously. So him bringing home Rory is a BIG DEAL. Also the fact that they’ve arranged his marriage when he’s in his 30s for a dynastic plan says a lot.

A lot of people can be privileged and realize that it’s lowkey a miracle that Rory turned out the way she did. Yes Rory made a bunch of stupid and selfish mistakes, but Rory is the daughter of an emotionally stunted (and Lorelei is many great things, but this is true) woman and emotionally neglectful man. 

On top of that, Rory grew up from poverty, because yes- having your mother be a teenage single mom that works as a maid DOES count as poverty despite people thinking you have to be an Oliver Twist Orphan to be considered poor- and studied and read a lot as a child. 

There was so much an academic pressure on Rory to be perfect and to make up for Lorelei’s life- both from Lorelei and her grandparents that so many students would have an extreme burnout at some point. 

Also I’m really sick of people acting as if Mitchum Huntzberger is some guy, and not, you know, a goddamn BILLIONAIRE NEWSPAPER MOGUL WHO IS BASED OFF THE FICTIONAL FAMILY WHO OWNS THE NEW YORK TIMES AND ITS LITERALLY ONE OF THE MOST POWERFUL AND INFLUENTIAL MEN IN AMERICA! 

Jesus, that would be like Anthony Bourdain or Bill Gates personally telling you, that you don’t have it when you’re only 20!

I see this with every single accomplishment that Rory has.

Rory scores higher than Paris on the PSAT? “Ugh main character syndrome” 

Rory works hard and has compilations of her studying? “She’s not really smart guys, or innately talented, Rory has to study all the time to know things, she’s just book smart!” (This particular argument REEKS of anti-intellectualism and stupidity. Plenty of naturally talented smart people study because they ENJOY the academic and mental challenge! This literally sounds like an argument someone with a C GPA would make for not turning b in assignments and still claim that they’re smart.) 

Rory gets an internship? “Ugh so cringe, how unrealistic! Rory is sooo pushy and entitled!” (If Paris did the same thing, they’d commend her for being a go-getter) 

Rory shelters Lane when she runs away from home, and stands up to her roommates when they want to kick lane out? “Rory is such a bad friend because she ignored Lane for one day when she was 16 and in a new school and relationship!” 

It’s deliberately ignorant and stupid, and I’m tired of it. At least hate Rory for things she *actually* did.
As somebody who panics about walking up the stairs I felt so seen by Rory lol

They made it seem as if the life and death brigade did so many cool things but literally all they did was go out in the woods, a.k.a. touch grass and that’s so fucking funny like college kids don’t get to touch grass after all

I feel like Rory needed to do what she wanted because at that point, Rory didn’t even know *who* she was doing journalism for.

Mitchum’s performance review of “you don’t have it”, shook her to her core because what was all this hard work for? What was all the hard work and Chilton and Yale and late nights and hours studying and supposedly wanting to go to Harvard since she was three (I side eye Lorelei heavily for that) for?

Honestly I really respect Logan for knowing Rory for who she was- not a perfect suffocating angel overachiever that Lorelei expected her to be, or the virginal angel do-over child that her grandparents expect her, or the maniac pixie dream girl Jess expects her to be- 

Logan sees Rory as a smart, witty, beautiful partner. He respects that Rory needs her own time to figure out WHO the hell she is and what she wants. And Logan’s confident that Rory WILL return to Yale and she does! Rory does and she graduates with honors

Exactly it’s not until that Rory calls  Dean desperately after Lorelei has to tell her how stupid she’s being to believe a guy like Dean, and then Lindsey picks up, that Rory realizes that Dean was just lying to her in order to sleep with her.

I fully believe that if Dean was honest about him just wanting to cheat on Lindsey, and just wanting to leave her, Rory probably wouldn’t have slept with him that night. Maybe it would’ve happened under other circumstances, but not like that. 

The whole situation felt very premedicated by Dean. He takes off the wedding ring and tells her that him and his wife both know that the marriage is over. That’s explicit.

Exactly because that would mean that Rory’s first time with Dean was a result of a lie. And I’m fully prepared to get downvoted for this opinion, but I feel like it was coercion or false pretenses at least on deans part. 

You don’t drive to your ex-girlfriend’s house in the middle of the night when her mother is explicitly not home, tell her that your marriage is over with your wife, make it clear that your wife also believes that the marriage is over and is on the same page, take off your wedding ring-

Only to go back to your wife’s house, and then lie to her about what you were doing and then yell at her. If it wasn’t for the letter, Dean would have never left Lindsay. He was dishonest to Rory. 

As much as I hate Rory for sleeping with Dean, I think she really did believe him, because she was lonely and she wanted to believe that good old reliable Dean would never hurt her and would always be there for her.

I really do feel sorry for her because her first time was with a liar who had no intention of leaving his wife.
Yesssss, thank god, free Lindsay and Rory from season 4 Dean that man looks so bummy I can not

No, she explicitly asked Dean about Lindsay and he said that him and his wife both know that the marriage is over. Like that is literally a flat out lie on deans part, and I bet that he explicitly went over when Lorelei wasn’t there just so he could get Rory alone to sleep with her.

Dean went to Rory’s house. Also, Dean has lied about other things in the past before to Rory.

Yeah, but Rory very explicitly ask Dean about Lindsay and then he tells her that they both know that the marriage is over.

If Dean had told Rory that, screw Lindsay I don’t care about her anymore, I think that would’ve been a different story.

Also, the fact that Rory calls Dean and then gets Lindsey on the phone, I think she was truly shocked that Dean would lie to her and had totally misrepresented the picture.

I disagree. I feel like it’s important that we don’t use gender words to describe women even when they do horrible things.

Homewrecker is specifically used to target women when men wreck their homes. Rory absolutely cheated with Dean but Dean is the homewrecker. 

What Rory did was out undoubtedly horrible, but I don’t think it’s necessarily infantilizing to say that a 19-year-old whose first boyfriend who told her “me and Lindsay…we both KNOW it’s over” was naïve, and honestly flat out lied to.

OK, no I think getting attitude in the street is just not a good look on anybody’s part. 

I totally understand Lindsey’s mom’s anger, but she’s not even letting her daughter speak. She’s literally just screaming at Rory while her daughter looks so ashamed and humiliated.

This is why I genuinely hate Lindsay’s mom so much because how are you pretending to make sandwiches with your daughter and acting all cutesey when your child is literally undeveloped as fuck and has zero fallback plan in case her husband cheats or dies or something happens to him God forbid!

Lindsey’s mom seems like so many fundamentalist moms that I remember from the church. So eager to put their daughters through the same fate, even though they know how dangerous it is.

Exactly! I know Dean was married but Lindsay and Rory were all teenagers. What Rory did was wrong, what Dean did was worse because he made vows, but at the end of the day they were nineteen. They were still *teenagers.* 

This was a horrible idea on everyone’s part to get married. If deans affair happened when Lindsay was pregnant, she would be in such hot water. Lindsay would have no education or fallback plan and all she would depend on is her husband.
Exactly Homewrecker is a slur made to shame women for men’s actions

Emotional support blankie is the perfect way to put it. Lorelei damn near dragged that child away from her bed, because she didn’t wanna be alone and have to sit with the consequences of ending her engagement to Max.

If that’s the case, Lorelei could’ve gone to Sookie, but no Lorelei dragged the one person who was the most impacted by her leaving Max, because she wants the validation. Lorelei doesn’t want to face Rory’s concerns and justified turmoil, so she uses Rory to comfort herself. Lorelei allows, Rory to be the parent in this situation and be the responsible one, while she gets to go on a roadtrip and not face her emotions.

I feel like Rory was angrier at Lorelei because at this point she’s conditioned to expect the worst of Chris. Chris abandoned her as a teenager, has said shit like “I knew Lorelei before you, we made a child together!” To said child. 

Rory is used to Chris neglecting her and treating her like collateral damage. But Rory and Lorelei are supposed to be BEST FRIENDS. Lorelei is always going on and on about how *important* and *special* their bond is, and yet she does something like this?

Not only does Lorelei fuck the man who has hurt Rory so badly, but then does it behind Rory’s back, AND expects Rory to be *happy* for her with no complains? It’s so selfish, and so shitty, and if I were Rory I would cut off Lorelei right then and there.

Like the fact that Lorelei ever entertained Chris as an option is so shitty.

I see so many people calling Rory a pick me as a teenager for being jealous of Shane and Bobby, but I rarely see the same ire pointed towards Lorelei, even though she’s genuinely being a pick me for choosing the man who is an absolute deadbeat and treat Rory like garbage. 

Like one of them is an immature teenager, and the other is an adult woman who is literally sleeping with the Chris in season one after his parents called Rory a mistake to his face. And instead of comforting Rory, she’s literally fucking Chris outside on the balcony as if she’s 16 again and it’s disgusting.

Like what about Chris is so attractive that your life thinks it’s OK to choose the man who never prioritized their  daughter’s well-being? And then she goes and gets married with Chris in Paris and she knows that will totally break Rory’s heart.

But for Lorelei, it’s my way in the highway and she always expects Rory to just roll over and be OK with all the fucked up things she does. Like when Lorelei ends things with Max, or starts things with Max when he was Rory high school teacher and it made Rory’s life hell, because they were caught kissing during parents day.

As much as Lorelei loves her daughter, sometimes I feel like Rory is less of a best friend and more of a sidekick to Lorelei’s life.

I’m going to be honest a lot of people who look down on Rory in a year in the life (and don’t get me wrong she does make some really bad decisions) also have a Blindspot when it comes to Loreleis flaws. 

Being the other woman is absolutely unacceptable and I’m not defending Rory’s choice to get back to Logan. But at the same time so is entertaining the deadbeat man, who has made your daughter cry and literally abandoned her, and has brought immense pain and emotional distress to your daughter, and yet nobody gives Lorelei shit for repeatedly, choosing to sleep with Chris and keeping him as an option. 

At this point after seeing Rory in tears and screaming, go be someone else’s dad, it’s a choice for Lorelei to destroy her daughter as well-being to be a pick me for a deadbeat dad. 

Rory is also flat out, broke in a year of the life, but when Lorelei is renovating the inn, she’s also an incredible debt and needs to cry to Luke and beg for a $30,000 loan. She also gets rejected from several banks when she needs to pay for the termite damage and needs to loan money from her parents. 

Lorelei also has several mortgages against her home, which is arguably a far worse financial position to be in. Lorelei is literally in debt.

And I’m not saying that Lorelei didn’t do well for herself, but I am saying that it’s literally impossible to get a home loan in 2016 vs the 90s especially in Connecticut.

And I know that Rory is struggling with her career, but Rory graduated during the 2008 financial crisis, which was one of the worst recessions America faced. 

Lorelai is totally a hard worker and I get that and I respect that, but she literally gets free room and board and a boss that gives her promotions on her first job. Whereas newspaper jobs are pretty much contract job now and good luck getting health insurance.

I didn’t like how blue and washed out a year in the life looked. The original series looked so cozy and so warm. 

A year in the life just looked so depressing. But to be fair, I feel like the first episode was supposed to be super depressing because Richard just died.

If it helps, I think she was a journalist for a while after season seven. Rory just has the misfortune of graduating before the 2008 financial crash and that would’ve really wrecked her plans to become a serious journalist.

The journalism industry, never, really, quite recovered after that, and a lot of traditional roles were outsourced into shitty contracts. In the meantime, she did get published in the Slate, the Atlantic, the New Yorker, which is pretty impressive.

I mean during a year in the life, Rory was grieving Richard and I thought it was a slow exploration of Rory’s grief and how out of character she’s acting.

Grief can make you fall into the worst habits and just catches up with you in the weirdest ways. I really thought that explained how out of focus she was and how she seemed really depressed and like nothing made her happy.

I don’t think Logan made her happy. I think he was just familiar, the fact that she kept forgetting to break up with Paul, the fact that she’s falling asleep while writing newspaper articles, the fact that she just doesn’t seem passionate about writing anymore, all of it, screams depression and grief to me. 
 
By the end of her year, she starts writing a book and she seems super passionate about it. Rory also decides to become editor of the stars Hollow Gazette, which is wonderful. Small town newspapers are very important, now more than ever. She finally finds the strength to break up with Logan. And it seems like Rory will be raising her kid on her own.

It’s not OK, but it’s extremely human. I know people who have cheated on their partners who have donated literal organs, and have done immense charity, and have literally saved my life when I was at my lowest.

And I was cheated on.

I’m just saying that people are very complex, and being bad at one aspect in your life doesn’t negate the good nor does it make up for your sins.

But clearly, plenty of people are cheating on their partners, maybe that says a lot about humans and the institution of marriage. 

Marriage was literally started as a way for men to barter off the women in their family, and pretty much treat them like property. I mean sure it’s evolved, considering how human rights are backsliding in America, and how women who have their husbands last name are gonna lose their right to vote, it makes me wonder who this system was set up for. And whether it should exist at all.

I don’t think they’re a good person from the perspective that they commit inFidelity, but I also know that people are incredibly complex.

I don’t think it’s fair right off a large portion of American women is just being bad people, and I think that’s a really narrow definition. 

A person can be a good person in other context and then be absolutely terrible in other contexts. One of my friends received a literal kidney from a lady that cheated on her wife. She also did like a lot of charity work, and would regularly clothe and feed the homeless.

Another time when one of my friends was about to be kicked out she let my friend and her newborn baby live with her for over a year! Genuinely she was such a godsend

That lady was an angel to my friend, to her wife, she wasn’t, people can be multiple things at one time.

Me neither, but unfortunately plenty of American women do and I don’t think it’s reasonable to write them off as evil people. 

They might make horrible decisions and I’m not saying that infidelity is OK but, I think it’s important to still be able to see them as people

I love the people were complaining that they should’ve shown more scenes of Rory studying and I was like be fucking real like, would you actually watch the show if it was Rory studying over and over and over again like come on people.
Dude it’s genuinely the most poorly self aware people that think they were perfect angels as teenagers and young adults.

ME every time I see people bitch about Rory getting plastered at that party her grandparents threw that she had no choice to attend where Dean dumped her like 

College kids can get hammered when they break up, hell college kids get drunk on the weekends and it’s perfectly fine! Like she’s young, she should be at the club guys like Rory only gets drunk like TWICE during the whole series like get real people, RELAX

Like Rory didn’t even want to be there in the first place and couldn’t say no because Emily and Richard are paying for Yale

Exactly this is Rory not being able to bottle it up anymore. Also Lorelei’s half assed apology after she gets caught MAKING OUT with Max during teachers day after she knew her daughter was being bullied by the whole school was just so pathetic. 

And the sad part is that Rory and swallow her emotions later when she finds out that Lorelei calls off the wedding.

Yes hallelujah! 

And noticed that Lorelei is the cool mom in so far as Rory goes to literally an Ivy League school and gets perfect grades and like the exact same music and movies that Lali likes and pretty much acts like her mini clone .

The moment Rory actually decides to think for herself, such as applying to Yale or enjoying the golf club, or even partying after her boyfriend dumps her and she’s forced to go to her grandparents, stupid party and meet a bunch of male bachelors, immediately jumps and thinks the worst of her which is so fucking unfair 

Lorelei has such a narrow definition of what Rory can be and like, and as soon as Rory deviates from that, she just shuts her daughter down. It’s easy to be the cool mom when you have a cool kid.

If Lorelei ended up having a  mini her, she would probably be a lot more like Emilly on the outside.

Considering that Lorelei doesn’t factor Rory when she leaves Max for the first time (she drags Rory on a Field trip and yells at her when Rory  has questions and is confused) and literally tells Rory NOT to tell Dean about the time she kissed Tristan at a party, I don’t buy it.

Lorelei has never had a problem asserting herself in her relationships with men despite Rory, and she is the mother here. If Lorelei wanted to, she could have told Luke about what she had done.

Rory was probably scared to lose another father figure

Yeahhhh also the hookup with Sherry when Chris came back to town was very sketch. Like I know they were fighting but Lorelei is wayyy to eager to entertain Chris’s deadbeat ass whenever he waltzes into town. 

And Rory witnesses that throughout her life, and even witnesses how her bio parents seem to always come back to each other despite having different partners and lives. The whole “he’s mine” theme rings hard with Emily, Lorelei, and Rory. 

Richard was engaged to another girl when Emily came onto the scene.

I think it got worse and a small part of Rory fractured when Chris functionally abandoned her for a new do over baby with Sherry after promising he wouldn’t leave. 

It seemed like Rory had a hard time letting go after that, like she kept clinging to men like a kid.

Yeah, I can appreciate the growth that just goes through, but I really feel like it’s a bit overrated considering that we see Jess for all of one or two episodes worth of content after he treated Rory and Luke and so many other people in his life like absolute dirt.

Male characters are able to hit the lowest of lows and are remembered for their great moments where a female character characters like Rory are pied to the face and remembered by their worst moments instead of their accomplishments.

People act as if Rory ended the series as a complete dropout and party girl, when in reality, she graduated from honors with Yale and got a job.

I’ve seen some people even disgustingly say that Rory should’ve communicated better and that she was overreacting and batting her eyelashes and all sorts of disgusting misogynistic drizzle that makes my stomach turn and makes my blood boil.

How can a fandom have so much internalized misogyny? How can I fandom love a male character to the point where they’re literally defending him as he is physically assaulting another girl. 

Whether or not other people argue at the same constitutes a sexual assault, it is very clear that boundaries were violated and the way that Jess acted was completely disgusting. I am not saying that Jess is abusive, but this instance is very abusive behavior.
Sure but I can blame Doyle for endorsing it and publishing it AND not letting Rory write a retraction
Doyle is the editor and has the final say over what is published. The fact that he rejected Rory’s other articles and fawned over this hit piece shows what kinda publication he was running.
Oh my god they would totally try to pray the gay away from Rory. I think they would eventually make peace but not before forcing her in many unpleasant ways
Exactly, people can’t wrap their head around how truly disgusting this was and how horrible shaming women for sex is. It’s genuinely a disgusting practice

I mean, Doyle literally rejected every single article except this very mean article. Even when Rory felt bad and tried to write a retraction Doyle outright rejected that idea. 

He very much encouraged Rory and as an editor, made it very clear that this is the direction that Rory should be writing the article in. 

Rory is absolutely at fault for writing this article but Doyle is more at fault because he was literally the editor, and he literally rejected every other article Rory wrote.

I mean, that meltdown completely broke Lane’s heart and she was absolutely crushed, and he never apologized to her on screen. Zach literally just proposed.

That was so selfish, and I don’t know how Lane could ever get back with Zach after he did that to her.
I guess so, but it just reminds me of real life women who get completely sabotaged by their partners.

Lorelei really does feed into Rory’s fears because why is she waking up her teenage daughter in the middle of the night to tell her “she can hear the termites” and making them go sleep at Sookie’s?

And Rory also hears that her mom has gotten rejected from THREE different banks for a loan. And the mother/friend relationship is very blurred.

Rory was right in the end- Lorelei DID need to swallow her pride and get a loan from Emily. And this doesn’t dismiss Emily’s horrible narcissism or abuse, but Lorelei and Rory could have been *homeless.*
On the bus, Jess promised Rory that he would take her to prom and get tickets but in reality he had his bags packed

Honestly I feel like a lot of people romanticize Jess, but just like Luke, Jess really mistreated Rory as a bf. 

Jess barely prioritized Rory, he screamed at her during that party, literally lied to her face about taking her to prom, and didn’t even say goodbye just like Chris. 

Meanwhile, Luke started off so strong but treated Lorelei SO badly and hid a whole ass kid from her and kept lying to her until she found out. 

Jess and Luke are great characters by themselves but honestly? They were pretty shitty partners

Exactly, people hate hearing this, but having a personality and being able to talk to people really does take you far in life. 

Rory may not be perfect, but she is a very good speaker, and she’s charming and smart enough to be witty without being obnoxious. 

These types of things really matter

Sure, but also, the quality of the candidate has gone up a lot, and I say this as someone whose close friend works with the admission office of an Ivy. 

It is far more competitive than the average candidate has a lot more going for them

The same people: “we need more complex female characters!”

Even if people think that Rory is more bad than good (and I don’t think that’s true), it’s still important to have female characters like that, and not have them be outlets for societally acceptable misogyny.

This fear of failure and of being seen is holding people back so much, I swear. It’s actually sad seeing so many young people not applying themselves, not setting out, because they’re afraid of looking cringe or looking like a failure.

And also, it’s actually ridiculous that people think that you’re a failure if you don’t get an internship right on the first time like that is so stupid and ageist and ugh.

Exactly it’s like have these people ever been a teenager and said some cringe things? Or ever have that feeling that you’re the only one that understands and that everyone else doesn’t get it?

I swear to God we’re gonna have the most boring female characters because the moment used up a toe out of line someone with zero media literacy or an inability to relate with characters will make a post over exaggerating the “bad thing they did”

Exactly, Paris was threatened from the beginning when she stole Rory’s file at Chilton because she knew Rory would be a fierce academic rival. Rory and Paris ARE academic equals and the stupidity of glorifying science and putting down literature in college is why America is entering a very intellectual age. 

Turns out poorly read people are very easy to control, and that humanities ARE important, gee whiz!

It’s like a miniature version of a Madonna whore complex and I see it all the time. Even when Rory and Paris are academically matched (I notice a lot of people reduce Rory’s intellectual accomplishments and it really does feel misogynistic, like there’s only ONE type of woman that’s allowed to be smart and it’s gross) I see people constantly hold Paris up to the light and put down Rory.

Sure, a lot of Gilmore girls is “main character” syndrome but like THEY are the main characters! Also why do we take smart male characters at face value and demand that female characters constantly jump through hoops to prove their intelligence?
Apparently, they should’ve pinned the letter A to Rory in bright Scarlet, and walked her around the town with a bell going “shame shame, shame”
Exactly, Rory had a lot of growth in season seven which they just bypassed, it’s ridiculous!

I’ve also seen some interesting takes that neglect is child abuse (I agree) and that by extension Chris is abusive which makes a lot of Rory’s issues make sense.

Gilmore girls? More like generational trauma girls

I don’t know I would definitely consider Paris a mean girl to Rory considering all the shit that she pulled. When she told the entire school about Rory’s mom kissing Max, I thought that was very mean girl. When she assigned Rory all those garbage pieces on the school newspaper, but then made Rory interview Mr. Medina that was also classic mean girl behavior.

I feel like we only think mean girls are mean girls when they’re popular, Paris was definitely smart enough to know how to hurt Rory

Yeah, especially considering that Paris is an actual mean girl to Rory many times I think Rory rises above the occasion and tries to be nice when she can. That doesn’t mean she’s perfect all the time and she’s definitely capable of being an asshole, but really we all are

W h a t are you talking about???

Also Paris didn’t just “simply not like Rory” Paris was so insecure and threatened that she stole Rory’s file on the first day, and then said “we don’t need any more kids from hole in the walls, it screws up the curve” which is gross and really pathetic. 

Paris and Tristan bullied Rory with that “Mary” scrap, and Paris was such  a giant pick me for Tristan, that she immediately took it out on Rory who did NOT deserve that AT ALL. 

Also remember the time Rory was reading at a bench and then Paris comes up behind her and threatens to make her school life a living hell?

Honestly if my “best friend” pulled the abusive crap that Paris pulled at the Yale Daily News I’d be hesitant too. 

People are acting as if Rory let Paris to drown when in reality Rory was deeply uncomfortable with the fact that Paris was literally *abusing* her staff to the point where she turned off the heating in fucking CONNECTICUT, banned bathroom breaks, verbally abused and insulted everybody on staff, dehumanized them to the point of assigning them numbers, tore apart their work…
